preferences: impl: model=opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash, thinkingOptionId=max, features.auto_accept=true, features.fast_mode=true, modeId=build
ui: provider=claude, model=claude-opus-5, thinkingOptionId=high (limited budget - reserve for copywriting, naming, UX copy, visual design, styling only)
planning: provider=codex, model=gpt-5.6-sol, thinkingOptionId=high (limited budget - reserve for high-value planning only)

audit: model=opencode-go/minimax-m3, thinkingOptionId=auto (lead reviewer - cross-family contrast from impl). For a second opinion, escalate to provider=codex, model=gpt-5.6-sol, thinkingOptionId=high.
vision: model=opencode-go/mimo-v2.5 (for image and video input)
deepseek-v4-flash is the primary workhorse with effectively unlimited usage. Use it for all impl, research, scheduled, and recurring work.

deepseek-v4-flash is also the orchestrator: it decides, synthesizes outputs, and delegates. When a decision needs frontier-model judgment, the orchestrator itself makes the call to provider=codex, model=gpt-5.6-sol for that one step, then resumes on deepseek-v4-flash.

Claude and codex budgets are limited. Reserve Claude (claude-opus-5) for human-skill work (ui) and codex (gpt-5.6-sol) for planning. Use them only when the task specifically requires their reasoning strength.
For audits and reviews, lead with minimax-m3. Bring in codex gpt-5.6-sol only as a second opinion when the first review is contested, high-stakes, or needs a different family's judgment.
For committees and second opinions, deliberately use a different model family than the primary agent to get genuine cross-model contrast.
Prefer asynchronous workflows. Set notifyOnFinish=true for all agent-scoped creates. Do not poll for completion.
Use workspace isolation (worktree mode) when running multiple agents in parallel on the same repo to prevent filesystem conflicts.
